newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends up as JGBs rise and stocks fall.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends up as JGBs rise and stocks fall.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen futures contract settled higher on Tuesday as buying ensued in line with a rise in Japanese government bonds and a fall in Tokyo share prices, traders said.
Concern about a possible rise in interest rates has waned considerably, and this is triggering buying of euroyen futures, they said.
The March's day session turnover was 64,213 contracts.

"Weak forecasts for industrial output in June and July released last week spurred buy backs, and euroyen futures were firm from early this morning, as the market carried over the sentiment," a brokerage house trader said.
Profit-taking was seen at around 98.93, however, and capped the March's rise, the trader said.
Traders said they expected the March to move in a range between 98.87 to 98.95 during the week.
The Bank of Japan, in a surprise move, injected 200 billion yen into the money market this morning.
The operation left the market with a fund surplus of 390 billion yen.

"Most in the market had expected the BOJ to leave a surplus of about 300 billion yen. But the BOJ probably decided they need to start pushing the rate lower in order to achieve their goal of keeping the key overnight call rate below the official discount rate on average," a city bank trader said.
The key overnight call money had been most actively traded at 0.49 percent as of 0600 GMT, but it was too early to say what the day's weighted average would be, a trust bank trader said.
The trust bank trader said it is possible that the day's weighted average may fall to 0.48 percent from the previous day's 0.52 percent.
"Judging from today's market conditions the BOJ will probably reduce the amount of surplus it leaves in the market tomorrow to 200 billion or 300 billion yen," the trader said.
About 180 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) had been issued at 0.70 percent, the highest rate since August 7, 1996, as of 0712 GMT.
One-month CDs were offered at 0.61 percent and two-month CDs were offered at 0.62 percent.

The rate for three-month CDs jumped sharply since they were last issued at 0.64 percent last Thursday, as issuers of the three-month CDs were eager to raise long-term funds to cover the end-September interim fiscal year-end, they said.
The rise in the key CD rate was due to such seasonal factors, and did not indicate that the market was becoming more worried about a possible rise in interest rates, traders said.

In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, Japanese banks were detected receiving three-year fixed interest rates, a city bank trader said. Three-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.48/52 percent as of 0722 GMT, down from Monday's 1.50/54 percent.
